avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

key_clinical_evidence: Cranial-nerve involvement (unilateral or bilateral) is common in severe AIDP and not equivalent to MFS or BBE.

patient.chief_complaint: Five-day progressive ascending limb weakness with global areflexia and new unilateral ptosis — no ophthalmoplegia, no diplopia.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. C. is a 57-year-old financial analyst presenting with a 5-day history of progressive bilateral limb weakness and numbness. On day 1 he noted bilateral limb numbness. By day 2 he had bilateral toe weakness. By day 5, weakness had progressed to involve both proximal and distal muscles of all extremities. He can no longer walk independently. He notices a new partial drooping of his left eyelid — this is an isolated unilateral ptosis without any diplopia and with full extraocular movements in all directions. He denies any recent respiratory illness, diarrheal illness, or viral syndrome. He has no dysphagia or dysarthria. He has no diurnal variation in his ptosis — it is present consistently throughout the day, does not worsen with fatigue, and does not improve in the morning. His blood pressure is elevated at 162/100 mmHg on admission. Hypertension was previously well-controlled on amlodipine. The isolated unilateral ptosis prompted workup for myasthenia gravis, Horner syndrome, and oculomotor nerve palsy, alongside the ascending limb weakness and global areflexia.

neurological_exam.additional: FVC: 2.4 L (predicted 3.8 L — 63%). NIF: -32 cmH2O. No diurnal variation in ptosis. No fatigability on upgaze testing. No recent infections recalled. BP 160/100 on admission. No respiratory or swallowing complaints.
neurological_exam.coordination: Intact on upper extremities. Lower extremity limited by weakness.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Partial ptosis of LEFT eyelid — partial drooping. RIGHT eyelid normal. Pupil size equal and reactive bilaterally. Extraocular movements FULL in all directions — no diplopia, no ophthalmoplegia. No facial weakness. No dysarthria.
neurological_exam.gait: Cannot walk independently. Bilateral lower limb support required.
neurological_exam.motor: Symmetric flaccid limb weakness: proximal lower extremity hip flexion 4/5, knee extension 3/5. Distal lower extremity ankle dorsiflexion 3/5. Upper extremity proximal 4/5.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Complete global areflexia — absent bilaterally in all four extremities.
neurological_exam.sensory: Bilateral numbness in glove-and-stocking distribution. Mild reduction in pinprick distally.
